key_insight: Putting a pretrained LLM inside a code sandbox lets it autonomously use the virtual computer (files, scripts, network) to solve non-code tasks—revealing general, agentic behaviors without extra training.
problem_solved: Limits of LLMs in handling long contexts, external knowledge acquisition, and flexible task execution are addressed by giving models a programmable environment they can explore and leverage.
method: Run the LLM interactively inside a code sandbox with capabilities to read/write files, execute scripts, and access external resources.
Let the model plan and perform multi-step interactions with the sandbox (e.g., fetch data, store context, run formatting scripts) without extra fine-tuning.
Use the file system and executed programs as external tools/memory to extend context length, obtain new knowledge, and automate task-specific processing.
impact: Practitioners can unlock more autonomous, reliable behaviors from existing LLMs by exposing simple programmatic environments—enabling longer-context handling, tool-driven pipelines, and reproducible automation without retraining.
visual_elements: Diagram: LLM ⇄ Sandbox loop showing file system, script execution, and network access arrows
Flowchart: example task (e.g., research summarization) showing steps—fetch resource → save to file → analyze → run formatter → output
Before/After bar or radar chart: capabilities (context length, external knowledge, formatting accuracy) with and without sandbox
Icon set: file system, terminal/execute, web fetch, brain/LLM to represent tools and emergent agentic behavior
paper_authors: Daixuan Cheng, Shaohan Huang, Yuxian Gu, Huatong Song, Guoxin Chen
